title: The Forecast tab prints module codes, the words 'Python' and 'handoff', and a raw code-bearing gap reason in reader text.
expected: D-12, D-13 part 2 and CM-012/CM-019: no CP- code, no 'handoff', no pipeline wording in sentences on a findings page; a standalone code in text is drawn as the module's name (ruling 2026-11-11, Amendment 2026-11-16).
actual: Model notes and limitations are drawn verbatim under the grid: 'LTM is the last fiscal year when that is the latest period CP-1 labels', 'Every figure is Python's arithmetic over inputs the CP-2G handoff stated', 'The last twelve months could not be built from the periods CP-1 prints'. A run-chart gap reason written 'Not established: see Filing p.12 for the trigger text (CP-4).' is drawn verbatim because containsReference matches file names, hashes and register ids only. The reader-facing strings 'The calculation gives X cash proxy. The handoff gives Y free cash flow' (Forecast.tsx:113), the button 'Open the forward credit handoff' (Forecast.tsx:270), 'The handoff does not bind a unique control...' (Downside.tsx:234), 'The handoff does not supply a pair of comparable last trades.' (Securities.tsx:274) and 'The handoff does not identify each event row.' (Calendar.tsx:38) and 'The handoff records a date gap in Evidence.' (Calendar.tsx:197, drawn on the calendar when a gap names a file) also use the pipeline word. No C4 component calls plainModuleNames or readerText. When the model carries a second grid ('Other forecast cases'), its column group is drawn as the store names it, 'Downside (CP-2G drivers)' (tests/test_credit_os_store.py:2076), so the module code heads a grid column; the cards and chart relabel the same case 'Downside drivers' (state reached by copying the grid in the browser). A run chart whose table the build rejected shows 'Leverage / Not established for this run / Sent back by the build.' (RunCharts.tsx:22; reached by marking the chart rejected in the browser).
suggested_change: Pass the notes, limits, chart-gap reasons and the degraded-state sentences through plainModuleNames/readerText; reword the delivery-written notes in cpos_forecast.py without 'Python' or 'handoff'; rename the button (for example 'Open the model evidence').

title: A gap ledger of ten near-identical limitation bullets is drawn on the Forecast findings page, and the same qualifications are drawn twice more.
expected: D-05 and CM-011: gap ledgers and registers are drawn only on Evidence and in the drawer; D-03: no flat repetition.
actual: Under 'Model limitations' the page lists one bullet per model line the forecast inputs do not name ('revenue: the forecast inputs do not name the row and period of this line', then EBITDA, cash interest, cash taxes, working capital change, capital expenditure, free cash flow, total debt, cash and cash equivalents, undrawn revolver). 'Not analytical review.' and 'Synthetic; not analytical review.' are drawn in 'Model scope and basis', again in 'Model limitations', and the unavailable rows repeat the same reason per cell when expanded.
suggested_change: Draw one sentence ('Ten model lines have no sourced starting value') with the names behind a trace control or on Evidence; do not repeat the scope passages in the limitations list.

title: Every trace control on the Forecast model opens the same drawer, titled 'Forecast inputs (machine-readable)', whose statement is generic.
expected: CM-008: the drawer lists the paragraph's Basis items with the figure's own source file, page, quoted passage and calculation steps; CM-009/CT-047: one control per figure leads to that figure's sources; CM-068/CM-272: the forecast-inputs block stays a delivery contract and is not shown.
actual: Model scope qualifications 1 and 2, the Base case and Downside shock cards, 'Cash flow model', 'Cash proxy by scenario' and the Revenue, Closing cash and Closing debt trend charts (8 of 8 tried) all open one drawer: title 'Forecast inputs (machine-readable)', subtitle 'Forward credit model · Handoff line 93', statement 'The model calculation uses the inputs recorded in this handoff.', one child 'Recorded forecast inputs'. The drawer says nothing about the figure that was opened and exposes the heading of the machine-readable block. The run charts, by contrast, open a drawer per chart.
suggested_change: Give each forecast figure its own trace (the grid row and period it draws, or the calculation row that produced it); retitle the drawer for the model, not the contract block.

title: The Debt stack, drawn when one facility has no balance, is a bar of coloured segments with no key that ties a colour to a facility.
expected: D-39 (no information by colour alone) and D-28/D-02 (a stack with a ranked legend, CM-127): each segment must be identified by a label or key.
actual: Two segments (blue and violet, from 'Senior secured term loan 1,200' and 'Senior notes 800') are drawn as <i role=img> boxes; the list below has the three names and amounts with no swatch, and there is no legend. A reader cannot tell which colour is which facility except by order and proportion; the ranking and cumulative leverage the handoff publishes are not drawn. The full StackChart path is used only when every facility has a balance.
suggested_change: Draw the same legend/ranked key as StackChart for the partial case (or pass the stated parts to StackChart and list the unstated facility as a gap row).

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (full), the Table form of every run chart
title: The Table form of each run chart leaves out the published 'Basis and limitation' column, so a row's limitation is shown only behind its trace control.
expected: CM-025 and D-28: every chart has a table form carrying the same published rows, unit, basis and source line, and the chart frame carries the module's basis note; AGENTS.md: every number and qualification exact.
actual: chartTable drops 'Source', 'Evidence' and 'Basis and limitation' whenever the evidence is in the drawer. All 10 table forms checked (Leverage, Interest cover, Liquidity, Debt maturities, Revenue and EBITDA, Debt stack, EBITDA bridge, Liquidity bridge, Refinancing need, Covenant headroom) show no basis; the handoff's rows carry 'Synthetic.' here and carry the real limitation of each figure in a live run. The text is reachable only by opening each row's drawer. This follows the voice standard (sources only in the drawer) but contradicts CM-025; the matrix and the code disagree.
suggested_change: Keep the Basis and limitation text beside the figure (a caption under the table or a quiet column) and leave only file and page references to the drawer; or amend CM-025.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (full), base case basis note (state: model unit USD millions, zero-input limitation)
title: The 'base case basis' sentence prints two figures without a unit and the third as '$62.00m', and its trigger text is emitted by nothing in the repository.
expected: D-15 and CM-022: every figure carries its currency or unit; one unit form across the page (CM-320).
actual: Rewritten in the browser from a model limitation and a Calculations ledger, the card reads 'The calculation gives 132.00 cash proxy. The handoff gives 194.00 free cash flow. The displayed difference is $62.00m.' The first two figures are unitless, the third uses '$...m' while the rest of the page says 'USD millions', and the sentence says 'handoff'. The branch needs a model limitation matching /machine input is set to zero/ and ledger rows 'Base FCF <FY>' and 'Base taxes and working-capital inflow <FY>': a search of src/, tests/ and docs/ finds the phrase only in web/src test fixtures, so no producer in this repository reaches it (branch that no current input reaches; if a live handoff does, the defects above apply). The canned run does not reach it; it was exercised with an intercepted snapshot (labelled state, not a live case).
suggested_change: Either remove BasisNote and the zero-input regexes if no handoff produces them, or draw all three amounts with withUnit(...) and drop 'handoff'.

title: One malformed date in a module's event table hides every event of that table, and the page says 'No dated events were published for this run' above a card saying the dates could not be plotted.
expected: D-31/D-14: a partial state is drawn as partial; the page must not claim there are no events when a module published them (CM-070).
actual: With the CP-2D table holding '2025-02-30 / day' and a valid '2025-06 / month' row, the calendar shows 'No dated events were published for this run.' followed by 'Financing', 'Liquidity', 'The recorded dates or precision could not be plotted.' The valid event is dropped (validatedEvents is all-or-nothing) and the headline sentence is false.
suggested_change: Plot the valid rows and list the rows that could not be placed; show 'No dated events' only when no table carries events or gaps.

title: The Chart/Table toggle is a radiogroup whose arrow keys move focus without selecting.
expected: D-35 and the ARIA radio pattern: arrow keys move focus and select in a radiogroup.
actual: With 'Chart' focused, ArrowRight moves focus to 'Table' while Chart stays aria-checked=true and the figure does not change; Space or Enter is then needed. Same on all 15 Forecast toggles and the Calendar toggle. The component is the shared ChartFrame (X1 owns the file).
suggested_change: Select on arrow (React Aria ToggleButtonGroup with a radio-style selection) or use role=group with aria-pressed buttons.

title: Trace controls share accessible names: three 'Show sources for Cash proxy by scenario', and 'Show sources for FY2023' (and FY2024, FY2026, FY2027) repeated across figures.
expected: D-37 and CM-009: one labelled trace control per row, each with its own accessible name.
actual: The chart header control and the two Scenario comparison rows (Base case, Downside shock) all read 'Show sources for Cash proxy by scenario' (the table passes the same `source` node to every row). Row controls in the Table form of the run charts are named by the row label alone, so 'Show sources for FY2023', 'FY2024', 'FY2026' and 'FY2027' each repeat across 2 to 4 figures (27 table-row controls checked; all open and return focus). The drawer also holds two buttons named 'Close' (the icon and the footer button).
suggested_change: Name each row's control by its case ('Show sources for Base case cash proxy').

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: a case's last cash proxy is not a value)
title: A case card whose cash proxy is missing reads 'Not available' with no reason, while the table beside it gives the reason and uses 'n.a.'.
expected: D-14 and CM-023/CM-066: a missing figure is 'n.a.' with its reason, never silent.
actual: With the Downside cash proxy cell set to na ('Not calculable: cash is negative before funding'), the card shows 'Not available'; only the Scenario comparison cell shows the reason.
suggested_change: Show 'n.a.' and the cell's reason on the card.

title: The yield value in the Securities comparison chart wraps its unit onto a second line and keeps four decimals.
expected: CM-022 (at most two decimals in prose) and D-32 (nothing broken): '7.0100%' should read on one line; the handoff gives '7.01% rounded'.
actual: The label is drawn '7.0100' with '%' on the next line (box 56 by 44 px, line height 22 px) beside a chart bar; the card above reads 'yield 7.0100%, 7.01% rounded'.
suggested_change: Draw the rounded text and widen the value column, or keep the unit with the number (no-wrap).

title: A lone 'x' is drawn under the Leverage and Interest cover charts as their unit note.
expected: D-16/D-26: unit notes read as words ('US$m', 'times').
actual: The figure caption is the one letter 'x' (Leverage, Interest cover) while money charts read 'US$m'; it looks like a stray character.
suggested_change: Label the unit 'x (times)' or show it in the axis title.

title: The same money unit is written four ways across the C4 screens: 'USD millions', 'US$m', '$m' and '$62.00m'.
expected: D-26 and CM-320: one unit form per report.
actual: Forecast model: 'USD millions' (or 'Units not recorded'); run charts: 'US$m' (as published); Downside, rate/FX and break-point comparisons: 'Stressed FCF ($m)', 'Change in debt ($m)' (unitLabel); basis note: '$62.00m' (withUnit).
suggested_change: Choose one rendering (the issuer's code plus 'm') and apply it through unitLabel/withUnit everywhere.

title: The calendar's year markers are 14 by 14 px, are not tab stops and cannot be pressed at 480 px or less.
expected: D-41: pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8) unless an equivalent control exists.
actual: 36 marker buttons measure 14 by 14 px, tabindex -1, pointer-events none at 390 px. The details row buttons (28 px) give the same information, so this is a polish defect.
suggested_change: Size the marker hit area to 24 px or drop the marker button role at narrow widths.

title: At 390 px the Scenario comparison table and the model grid are clipped without a scroll cue, and the Scenario comparison region is not keyboard-reachable like the model grid.
expected: D-42 and D-35: content reflows without loss; a scrollable region is focusable and named.
actual: Scenario comparison has scrollWidth 420 in a 316 px box (the FY2027E column is cut off) with tabIndex -1 and no role or label; the Cash flow model container is role=region, labelled and tabIndex 0. Published exposures (inside the closed details) uses the same ChartTable wrapper. The model grid at 390 px also shows two of three forecast years (its sticky 'Line item' column takes about 45% of the width) and cuts FY2027E in half with no fade or hint that the region scrolls; its container is focusable and named, so the keyboard path exists.
suggested_change: Give the ChartTable wrapper role=region, an aria-label and tabIndex 0 when it overflows.

title: Chart axis labels (131 SVG text nodes on the Forecast tab), the limits chart labels and the 'On this page' label are 12 px.
expected: D-30: no text under 13 px.
actual: Computed font size is 12 px for every chart axis label, 'limit 2.50%', '2.37%', 'Max single issuer exposure' and 'On this page'.
suggested_change: Raise the chart label size to 13 px; use text-small for the nav label.

title: The Forecast 'On this page' marker follows clicks only, so aria-current can name a section the reader has scrolled away from.
expected: Code read: state set and never reconciled with the viewport.
actual: ForecastNavigation sets `active` on click only (Forecast.tsx:281-287); scrolling by wheel or keyboard leaves aria-current on the last button pressed.
suggested_change: Drop aria-current, or track the section in view.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: duplicate or more than six case names)
title: Two columns with the same case name, or more than six cases, silently lose the cash proxy chart or the case cards.
expected: D-31: a degraded state is stated.
actual: With a duplicated 'Base case' group the Base case card reads 'Not available' and the chart draws only the Downside shock; with seven cases the case choice and the Cash proxy chart disappear with no note. Parked under R3 (hostile input).
probe: C4_STATE=dup-case C4_CHARS=3000 node docs/audit/2026-11-16-final/output/2-sections/C4/probes/c4-states.cjs; C4_STATE=many-cases C4_CHARS=3000 node docs/audit/2026-11-16-final/output/2-sections/C4/probes/c4-states.cjs
suggested_change: Say 'The cases could not be drawn on a common basis' instead of dropping them.

title: The Forecast tab shows no case drivers on the case cards and no deleveraging or break-point timing; drivers appear only as grid rows and the assumptions sit in a closed details.
expected: CM-065 (forecast cases with their drivers), CM-165 (driver comparison), CM-164 (deleveraging and break-point timing on Forecast).
actual: Cards show cash proxy, period, unit and the note only. 'Forecast assumptions' is closed by default and, for the canned run, holds only 'Observed / Not supplied: nothing to report'. T2H.7 and T2H.8 are not drawn on the Forecast tab at all (only model.register, T2H.3, is). The synthetic run holds no driver data, so the exact gap for a live run is not verified.
suggested_change: Name the driver basis on each card and draw the break-point timing, or amend the matrix.

title: Period series (leverage, interest cover, liquidity) are drawn as grouped columns; a line is used only when a value is negative.
expected: D-02 and CM-122/123/124: a trend as one line (C2) or multi-series paths (C3).
actual: periods() returns TrendChart only when `values.some(v < 0)` (charts.tsx:97); otherwise ColumnsChart. Two periods read acceptably as columns; with several periods a line would show the path the matrix asks for.
suggested_change: Choose the form from the descriptor's kind (trend) rather than from the sign of the values.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: no validated portfolio basis; a covenant with no stated threshold or a negative current value)
title: An undrawable chart is drawn as 'Source table available...' plus the raw table, not the gap panel, and one covenant row with no threshold removes the bullet chart for every test.
expected: D-14 and CM-021/CM-071: a missing chart is a hatched gap panel with the reason ('unevaluated position stays a gap').
actual: With /connected/portfolio returning {basis: null} (or 404) the Portfolio limits card shows 'Source table available. This report does not record a validated portfolio basis for a chart.' and the full table with its 'Reporting unit' column. With the CP-4 table's first threshold 'Not supplied: not stated', or a negative current value (net cash), the Covenant headroom chart for all three tests is replaced by 'Source table available. The chart could not be drawn on a common basis.' and the table; the two valid rows are not drawn. No GapPanel is used in either state, and the sentences use 'report' and 'basis' in the pipeline sense.
suggested_change: Use GapPanel with a plain reason ('The portfolio limits could not be checked against the mandate for this run').

title: The 'Published model' selector names models 'Model 1 · candidate' using the builder's mode word.
expected: D-16 and CM-019: plain, reader-facing names.
actual: With a second model the select options read 'Model 1 · candidate' and 'Model 2 · alternate'.
suggested_change: Name models by case and date.

title: The 'Compare with the 5% move' control is a select with a single option ('10%').
expected: A control offers a decision (D-35, control matrix: the user can decide exactly what the row says and nothing else); Securities guards with `quotes.length > 2`.
actual: FxShocks draws the select whenever two moves compare; with exactly two moves the only alternative is 10%, so choosing does nothing. Downside.tsx and the rate selector use the same pattern.
suggested_change: Draw the select only when there are two or more alternatives; otherwise state the comparison in the chart subtitle.

title: The same stress case is named 'Downside shock' on the card, chart and comparison table and 'Downside case' in the grid header.
expected: D-26/D-16: one name per case across a screen.
actual: forecastCaseLabel maps 'Downside case' to 'Downside shock' only for cards and the cash proxy chart; the grid group header (and the 'Downside drivers' label for a second downside) keep the stored name.
suggested_change: Apply forecastCaseLabel to the grid's column group labels.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: the model matches no single forward-credit handoff)
title: When the published model cannot be matched to exactly one forward-credit handoff, every trace control on the Forecast model disappears and the page does not say so.
expected: CM-009/CT-047: one trace control per figure; AGENTS.md: missing handoff content remains an explicit gap, never a silent absence.
actual: forecastHandoff returns undefined unless exactly one CP-2G output matches; `source` is then undefined and ForecastCases, ForecastScope, CashProxy, the trend charts and the grid draw no control (26 controls become 13, the run charts' own). 'Forecast evidence and artifacts' falls back to '#evidence/summary'. Nothing on the page says the sources are unavailable. Reached by rewriting the model's `download` field in the browser (a rerun or a second CP-2G output would do it).
suggested_change: Draw a quiet gap line ('Sources for the model are not linked in this run') and a link to Evidence when the handoff is not unique.

title: One long unbroken word in a model note, limitation, case description or scenario anchor widens the whole report page.
expected: D-32 and D-42: long text wraps in full and never pushes the page wider than the window; a qualification is not truncated.
actual: A 220-character word (a long path, hash or URL would do) in a Forecast note, a Forecast limitation or a case description makes #main 1,971 px wide in a 1,372 px area; in the Downside scenario fields 150-character words give 1,922 px (1,210 px at 390 px). Header, tabs, cards and charts all stretch and the right half is off screen. The note and limitation lists are plain <li>, the case description a plain span, the Downside definition list a plain <dd>; Securities cards use wrap-anywhere and the calendar uses break-words, so the pattern exists but is not applied here. Parked under R3 (unusual input).
suggested_change: Add wrap-anywhere (overflow-wrap:anywhere) to the note and limitation lists, the case description and the Downside definition values; give the report column min-w-0.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: chart amounts in other typographic forms)
title: A chart amount written with a typographic minus, parentheses, a space or no-break space as thousands separator, or a unit suffix removes the whole chart, while Downside reads the typographic minus.
expected: D-31: one unreadable cell should not lose the chart; D-26: one number grammar across components (Downside.position and MacroSensitivity.moneyPosition normalise U+2212).
actual: amount() in visuals/visualData.ts accepts only an ASCII hyphen-minus and comma-grouped digits. With 'Disposal' written '−10' or '(10)', the EBITDA bridge is replaced by 'Source table available. The chart could not be drawn on a common basis.' and the table; the same for the Liquidity bridge with '−450' and for Revenue written '2 100' or '2,100m'. The fallback is safe (no wrong figure is plotted) but the chart is lost; the module text uses U+2212 elsewhere (proof/handoffs/CP-2A.md T2DS.4).
suggested_change: Normalise U+2212 and parenthesised negatives in one shared parser (as Downside already does) and keep rejecting anything else.

title: A published value written with a decimal comma ('3,75') is read as 375 and its bar is drawn at 375 beside 2.80.
expected: D-15 and AGENTS.md: exact amounts; a value that is not a valid number is a gap, never a different number.
actual: amount() matches /^-?\d[\d,]*(\.\d+)?$/, so any comma placement is a thousands separator. With the first Leverage cell '3,75' the y axis runs to 400 and the bar is drawn at 375 while the other bars sit near zero; the label still reads '3,75'. The same parser feeds every period, stack and waterfall chart on the Forecast tab. Parked under R3 (malformed input).
suggested_change: Require thousands groups of exactly three digits (^-?\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+(\.\d+)?$|^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$) and treat anything else as not plottable.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast (partial: a model with an 'Upside' or 'Downside (CP-2G drivers)' case)
title: A case whose display name differs from its stored group name shows 'Case description not recorded.' although the model's note for it exists.
expected: CM-065: each forecast case is drawn with its recorded description.
actual: caseDescription builds the note prefix from the display label (`${name} is`), special-casing only 'Downside shock'. With an 'Upside' group and the note 'Upside is the optimistic case...' the card is 'Upside case' with 'Case description not recorded.'; the 'Downside drivers' card behaves the same. The canned run has neither group, so this was reached by rewriting the model in the browser.
suggested_change: Look the note up by the stored group name and show the display label separately.

screen: /report/<run>#calendar (partial: an event name that contains a file name)
title: An event whose name contains a file name is drawn as 'See Evidence', so the reader cannot tell which event it is.
expected: CM-070/D-12: the event is named in words; only the reference is withheld.
actual: eventDisplay replaces the whole cell with 'See Evidence' when containsReference matches, for the date-published, event and relevance columns. With 'Redemption notice per notice_of_redemption.pdf' the row and the Table form read 'See Evidence' and nothing else about the event. Reached by rewriting the event table in the browser.
suggested_change: Strip only the file name ('Redemption notice') or draw the event with its trace control.

title: While the portfolio basis is loading the Portfolio limits card states that the report records no validated basis.
expected: D-31: a loading state is shown as loading; a gap is stated only when the answer is known.
actual: PortfolioBasisProvider supplies null until /connected/portfolio answers, so the card draws 'Source table available. This report does not record a validated portfolio basis for a chart.' and the raw table, then swaps to the chart (3.5 s in the delayed state; one or two frames on a fast local service).
suggested_change: Draw nothing (or a quiet loading line) until the basis request settles.

title: Each Recharts chart is an extra tab stop with role=application, named only by its title, with an empty description.
expected: D-44 and D-28: a chart has a name, a short description (kind of chart and what it shows) and the table form as the full alternative; D-35: no pointer-only information.
actual: 12 chart surfaces carry tabindex=0, role=application, <title> equal to the figure title and an empty <desc>; no figure has aria-describedby. Keyboard users tab through 12 stops; ArrowRight then shows a visual tooltip ('FY2026E / Base case / 1,092') that is not announced. The Table toggle holds the same values, so this is a polish defect.
suggested_change: Describe each chart in its <desc> (kind, periods and range) or drop accessibilityLayer and rely on the Table toggle.

title: Three Forecast branches match limitation text that nothing in src/ writes: the zero-input basis note, the base-period and base-interest qualifications.
expected: Code read (brief check 5): a branch is reached by some producer, or is removed.
actual: BasisNote and recordedBridge need 'machine input is set to zero' and 'Base FCF <FY>' ledger rows; ForecastTable's Qualification needs limits starting 'Base period is ' or 'Base interest is '; scopePassages keeps limits matching /machine input.*zero/. A search of src/ finds none of these strings; they appear in web/src/**/*.test.tsx fixtures and in the UI only. They may match text a module writes into the CP-2G handoff (not verifiable offline), so this is an observation for stage 6, not a defect.
probe: grep -rn "machine input\|Base period is\|Base interest is\|Base FCF" src --include=*.py
suggested_change: Confirm with the CP-2G method text which limitations the module writes; delete the branches no producer reaches.

screen: /report/<run>#forecast > #modules/CP-6 (module link above a run chart group, 1440)
title: Following a module link at the foot of the Forecast tab opens the module page scrolled part-way down, its title and bottom line off screen, with focus left on the page body.
expected: Opening a page starts at its top and moves focus to the page (D-38 focus moves in on navigation; D-22 one clear first thing per screen).
actual: From the 'Committee decision' link under Run charts (Forecast scrollTop 6,926) the Committee decision page opens at scrollTop 2,192 of 3,092 with its heading at y = -1,893 px; the reader sees the end of the Statements and records section and must scroll up to find the bottom line. document.activeElement is BODY. The scroll position belongs to the shared <main> scroller, which no hash change resets (ReportLibrary only re-renders on hashchange); Overview > Open issuer calendar happened to land at 0. The five module links in RunCharts are the C4 instances; the cause is in the report shell (C1).
suggested_change: On a tab or module change, set main.scrollTop = 0 and move focus to the page heading (the shell already does the second on the start page).

title: The FY2027E cash proxy reads 172.46 on the case card, chart and Scenario comparison and 172 in the model grid directly below.
expected: D-15 and CM-022: the same figure reads the same on one screen, two decimals at most.
actual: Base case FY2027E cash proxy is drawn '172.46' (card, chart label, Scenario comparison) and '172' (grid row 'Cash proxy (not issuer free cash flow)'); FY2026E is '152.64' against '153'. The grid shows the model's published display (no decimals), the card and comparison use the exact value rounded to two places. Both are faithful to the model; the screen shows one figure in two precisions.
suggested_change: Use the grid's published display on the card and comparison, or label the card 'to 2 decimals'.

title: The break points are re-ordered by delivery (smallest required EBITDA decline first) and drawn as an ordered list, a ranking the module did not write for this table.
expected: D-47 and AGENTS.md: delivery adds no analysis; it selects and orders module-written passages. A first-break ranking is analysis unless the module wrote it (the 'First-break ranking' table).
actual: orderedRows sorts every row by its required decline, missing values last. For the retained T2DS.6 table (B1 FCF reaches zero, B2 Cover reaches watch level, B3 Net leverage watch level, no rank column) the page lists B2 before B1 on the k = 0.05 basis (0.12 before 0.20) in an <ol>, so the reader reads 'Cover reaches watch level' as the first break. The caption says 'Longer bars indicate a smaller EBITDA decline'. The ordering is delivery's own.
suggested_change: Keep the handoff's row order for T2DS.6 and rank only when the module wrote a 'First-break ranking'; or record the ordering as a ruled presentation.

title: At 390 px the EBITDA bridge's x-axis labels touch or overlap ('Restructuring add-back', 'Disposal', 'Issuer-adjusted EBITDA').
expected: D-42 and D-32: text does not collide at 390 px; labels wrap or rotate.
actual: Adjacent label boxes are 1 px and 2 px apart, and 'Disposal' overlaps 'Issuer-adjusted EBITDA' by 2 px; the labels run together ('RestructuringDisposalIssuer-adjusted' to a screen reader reading the SVG text). The same bridge at 1440 px is clean; the Liquidity bridge's longer labels wrap cleanly in two lines.
suggested_change: Wrap the waterfall category labels to the column width with a minimum gap (as WrappedAxis does for the other charts).
